question: If salvation is by works, what do you offer someone who has failed?
subtitle: The pastoral question. This is where the room is actually won or lost.
aliases: be perfect as your Father is perfect
what do you say at a funeral
finding: Everything, and it arrives faster than the transaction model allows. Jesus forgave people on the spot, repeatedly, before any restitution, without an altar, without a priest, and without a drop of blood, and he did it for the worst-positioned people in his society. Our position has never been that you earn God's welcome by accumulating good deeds. It is that the welcome is free and the life that follows is real. Repentance is metanoia, a turn, and it is available in a second to anyone still breathing. A man dying on a cross beside him cleared the threshold with nothing left to give. What we do not offer is a mechanism that makes the turning optional. The father runs the whole distance, and the son still gets up and walks home.
oneLiners: "What do you offer the man who failed?" The same thing Jesus offered the man dying next to him. Everything, immediately, for nothing.
The father ran. Before the apology finished, before a cent was repaid, before anybody bled.
Seven words from a tax collector and he "went down to his house justified." That's Jesus's word, not ours.
We don't say your debt was transferred. We say it was dropped.
Jesus isn't a payment we bank. He's a pattern we join, and he went first.
doNotSay: Don't lean on John 8:11 as bedrock. The pericope adulterae is absent from the earliest manuscripts; say so before someone else does. The case doesn't need it.
Don't run the calculation at a funeral. Asked for the headcount, Jesus declined and told the asker to mind his own door (Luke 13:23-24).
Don't read "be perfect" as flawless. Teleios means complete; the context (Matthew 5:43-48) is loving without excluding anyone, the way the sun doesn't.

sources.phrase: shalt thou be with me in paradise
sources.note: A condemned man, hours to live, no works possible, no creed, no sacrifice, no baptism. One sentence, and a promise with "today" in it. The floor of our position: whatever the threshold is, he cleared it with nails through his hands.

sources.phrase: when he was yet a great way off
sources.note: The father sees him far off, runs, and the embrace lands before the prepared speech. No ledger, no penalty, no third party absorbing the debt. The father simply eats the loss.

sources.phrase: God be merciful to me a sinner
sources.note: Seven words, and Jesus uses the justification word, dedikaiōmenos, of the collaborator with nothing to show. Not of the man with the compliance record, who is in the story specifically because he had one.
Direct forgiveness, no altar, no priest, before Golgotha. Also Luke 7:48. If blood were the mechanism these scenes are impossible. The cross did not open a door Mark 2 shows already open.

sources.phrase: This day is salvation come to this house
sources.note: Jesus invites himself to dinner first. Zacchaeus's restitution is his response, not his admission fee. Welcome, then transformation, then the verdict: our entire soteriology acted out in nine verses.

sources.phrase: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion
sources.note: Forgiveness is received by participating in it (also Matthew 6:14). Forgiving someone is a thing you can do today, from anywhere, owning nothing. The servant is condemned for refusing to pass on what he had already been given free (18:27).

sources.phrase: when saw we thee an hungred
sources.note: Both groups ask the same stunned question; neither had a tally. The currency is food, water, a coat, a visit: the smallest denominations of mercy. Nobody is priced out.

sources.title: Didache 6:2
sources.note: The oldest surviving pastoral instruction in Christianity. Not "meet the standard." "If you cannot bear the Lord's full yoke, then do what you can."

sources.phrase: this poor widow hath cast more in
sources.note: Two coins outscored the large gifts. The measure is proportional, not absolute. A sick person is not a disqualified person; they are usually the one Jesus is standing next to in the story.

"An impossible standard, which is exactly why you need substitution." Take it seriously. Teleios means complete, brought to its intended end, and the context is loving enemies because the sun rises on the evil and the good. A horizon, not a bar. The earliest Christians read it and immediately added: if you cannot, do what you can.

Say the textual status out loud before someone else does: John 7:53-8:11 is absent from the earliest manuscripts and floats between locations in later ones. We cite it as early, treasured tradition, not bedrock. Luke 23:43 and 15:20 are not in doubt by anyone.

sources.phrase: the works that I do shall he do also
sources.note: "Then what is Jesus to you? You've emptied him out." The opposite: a mechanism is a smaller thing than what he is. He shows what a human fully aligned with God looks like under maximum pressure, and says that was the point. Theosis: "partakers of the divine nature" (2 Peter 1:4), "that they all may be one" (John 17:21). Not a payment we bank; a pattern we join.

sources.phrase: are there few that be saved
sources.note: "What do you say at a funeral?" We say the person is held, that God "is not the God of the dead, but of the living" (Mark 12:27), and that the measure was mercy. We don't run the calculation; asked for the headcount, Jesus declined and told the asker to mind his own door.
